correctness.rationale: An entry with two lower entries to its right creates 321 or 312. Conversely a binary positional Lehmer word avoids both; a run of k ones followed by a zero uses the next k+1 consecutive values in the relative order (2,3,...,k+1,1). These blocks are ordered by value, so 2341 occurs exactly when some k>=3. Append the forced last zero. At adjacent positions i,i+1 a following zero means the two entries are the two smallest remaining and the swap toggles just b_i. A following one means the second entry is third smallest at step i, so exchanging produces a digit two. Under the resulting right-zero rule each mismatch needs a flip and each forced common one needs two. In the reverse removal and forward insertion sweeps each facilitating neighbor is already zero or still zero, and intermediate words lie coordinatewise below the respective endpoints. This works for every downward-closed binary family and gives precisely |M|+2|F|. In the 111-free case a forced common one has an immediately preceding mismatch: the first forced common one after a mismatch cannot be followed by another forced one without violating 111 in one word. Two forced positions two apart would have word types D-(B or C)-D, with the middle one in an endpoint sharing both D positions, again violating 111. Thus forced positions start at index at least two and are spaced by at least three, giving |F|<=floor((m+1)/3). The (BDC)^h construction with suffix empty, B or BD according to m mod 3 is 111-free in each projection, with all non-D positions mismatches and every D forced; this includes m=1 and 2. The asserted sharp diameter follows. VERIFICATION.md and verify.py were read, not executed; the bounded BFS and direct permutation enumeration described therein are corroboration, not the proof. Replay from RESULT.md lines 25–49; there is no claim for arbitrary adjacent-value moves or general forbidden runs.

evidence: Every weak-order descent from a restricted word swaps an adjacent descent; in the block description that swaps the last two entries of a block, toggling a one to zero and remaining in the class. Thus the restricted class is a lower weak-order ideal and the prior saturated descent/ascent through the meet stays in the restricted graph.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: It follows that the restricted metric equals the prior meet distance, not merely that it is bounded below by it. At code level each maximal one-run with start p encodes value inversions (p+1,p),(p+2,p),... along that run; the intersection of two such sets retains the shared ones of aligned runs, i.e. exactly the unforced common ones. Thus |M|+2|F| is an explicit evaluation of the earlier metric here. Its sharp maximum still requires proving that forced positions pack every third coordinate at most and that all length residues admit extremizers. The Gray listing and both known other diameter formulas do not supply that step.

value.rationale: The known adjacency listing establishes a navigable class but gives no sharp worst case. The forbidden run changes exact move complexity on a natural pattern class: the obstruction is propagation of common ones, but 111 forces these obstructions to be separated by three. Packing and explicit extremizers explain the diameter's linear slope and period rather than just computing examples. Value rests on that restricted optimization, not on restating the known meet metric or the unrestricted 2n-3 result.
